subproblem.title: Push-forward by the identity is the identity
subproblem.statement: Let lpush be any family of maps lpush_{N,N',k} : (ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}), one for all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, where 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k. Suppose lpush satisfies (PA): take N, N', k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, Λ' ∈ ℝ, a Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, a sequence of maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with spt X compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) and a sequence η_j ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N). If every F_j is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), ‖fderiv ℝ F_j x‖ ≤ Λ' for all j and x ∈ spt X, F_j → F uniformly on spt X (TendstoUniformlyOn), and for every j there is an open W ⊇ spt X with η_j(x) = (ω(F_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F_j x) for all x ∈ W, then X(η_j) → lpush_{N,N',k}(F, X)(ω). Conclusion: for all N, k ∈ ℕ and every X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with spt X compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞, lpush_{N,N,k}(fun x => x, X) = X.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (lpush : ∀ (N N' k : ℕ), (Euclid N → Euclid N') → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) k), (∀ (N N' k : ℕ) (Λ : NNReal) (Λ' : ℝ) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N') (Fs : ℕ → Euclid N → Euclid N') (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) k) (ηs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k), LipschitzWith Λ F → IsCompact X.support → X.mass < ∞ → boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ → (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (Fs j)) → (∀ j, ∀ x ∈ X.support, ‖fderiv ℝ (Fs j) x‖ ≤ Λ') → TendstoUniformlyOn Fs F atTop X.support → (∀ j, ∃ W : Set (Euclid N), IsOpen W ∧ X.support ⊆ W ∧ ∀ x ∈ W, (ηs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (Fs j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (Fs j) x)) → Tendsto (fun j => X (ηs j)) atTop (𝓝 (lpush N N' k F X ω))) → ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k), IsCompact X.support → X.mass < ∞ → boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ → lpush N N k (fun x => x) X = X
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix N, k and X with spt X compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞. By GeometricCurrentOn.ext it suffices to show lpush_{N,N,k}(id, X)(ω) = X(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N).
2. Apply (PA) with N' := N, Λ := 1, Λ' := 1, F := id, F_j := id for all j, this X, this ω, and η_j := ω for all j. The hypotheses hold:
- id is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.id), and X satisfies the three normality hypotheses.
- id is C^∞ (contDiff_id).
- fderiv ℝ id x = ContinuousLinearMap.id (fderiv_fun_id), whose norm is ≤ 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le).
- The constant sequence id converges uniformly to id on spt X (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff, since dist(x, x) = 0 < ε).
- Take W := univ, which is open and contains spt X. For every x, (ω(id x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ id x) = (ω x).compContinuousLinearMap (ContinuousLinearMap.id) = ω(x): rewrite with fderiv_fun_id, then check on vectors (ext; simp), since id ∘ v = v.
3. (PA) says the constant sequence X(ω) tends to lpush(id, X)(ω). It also tends to X(ω) (tendsto_const_nhds). By uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique), lpush(id, X)(ω) = X(ω). □

Lean proof script. It compiled with lake env lean after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, inside namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens, and uses no interface. It is the tactic body of theorem Submission.cmcdt_lpo_pf_identity : <lean_statement> := by
  intro lpush hPA N k X hX1 hX2 hX3
  ext ω
  have hU : TendstoUniformlyOn (fun (_ : ℕ) (x : Euclid N) => x) (fun x => x) atTop X.support := by
    rw [Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff]
    intro ε hε
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun j x _ => by simpa using hε
  have hT := hPA N N k 1 1 (fun x => x) (fun _ => fun x => x) X ω (fun _ => ω) LipschitzWith.id
    hX1 hX2 hX3 (fun _ => contDiff_id)
    (fun j x _ => by rw [fderiv_fun_id]; exact ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le) hU
    (fun j => ⟨univ, isOpen_univ, subset_univ _, fun x _ => by
      rw [fderiv_fun_id]
      ext v
      simp⟩)
  exact tendsto_nhds_unique hT tendsto_const_nhds
proof_key_steps: By ext, fix a test form ω.
Apply (PA) with F = F_j = id, Λ = Λ' = 1 and η_j = ω, using id^#ω = ω.
The constant sequence X(ω) tends to both lpush(id, X)(ω) and X(ω), so they are equal.

audit.reason: Constant identity approximants satisfy every PA hypothesis, including the derivative bound in dimension zero. Uniqueness of limits and current extensionality prove the exact identity conclusion.
